chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Cafe Society opening in 1938 as the first integrated New York club
summary: Stewart was about to leave for the Coast in 1938; Crouch relays Barney Josephson's account that other clubs admitted Black musicians but not Black patrons.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Maybe so. Now, do you -- were you in New York when the Cafe Society opened up or were you on the road?
I probably was. What year was that?
Cafe Society opened in 1938, December.
1938. I was just getting ready to leave New York, if I remember, to go out to the Coast.
Were the guys talking about the opening of the club since it was the first integrated nightclub in New York?
Well, I didn't notice that. I wasn't out in the, what I mean, myself personally, I wasn't around when I would hear a statement on that order where the club was an integrated (inaudible).
But you were aware of the fact that there weren't integrated jazz clubs in New York.
Oh yes, right.
Right.
Right, I had heard, you know.
Yeah, because -- that's right because you had just begun to start working as a professional around that time.
That's right, yes.

Because when I was talking to Barney Josephson about it, he was saying that the reason he opened the club was that all of the clubs that he went to, other than like certain kinds of after-hours spots, --
Yes, right.
-- that black musicians could work in the clubs --
Could work in the clubs.
-- but black patrons weren't --
Patrons, yeah.
-- allowed in any of them. I think he said the Kit-Kat Club --
Kit-Kat, yeah.
He named a bunch of clubs, the names of which I can't recall right now.
Around New York City.
Yeah. That you could go -- you could stand there and play and waitress in there.
Oh sure, yeah.
You could even be a maitre'd, --
That's right.
-- but if you came up to the door and tried to come in there to sit down --
Tried to come in, right.
-- and listen to the music, it wasn't happening.
That's right.
